content.comment_body: Has anyone used microSD cards with [product_name]? Which type is most reliable for this application? Is it possible to use larger cards (4GB or 8GB) if formatted to 2GB, and can microSDHC or microSDXC cards be used? Thanks for any advice.

The cards should be formatted using FAT32. I tested SDHC cards myself, including a 16GB and another type mentioned elsewhere in the forum. For example, I tried SanDisk and Verbatim microSDHC cards. According to [company_name] support, only SD cards with FAT32 are officially supported. SDHC cards were not thoroughly tested and may cause issues.
I'm using a microSDHC card and it works well with 2GB.

I use a Transcend microSD card with a 2GB capacity. When formatted with FAT32 and the default cluster size, [product_name] does not seem to recognize the card. Do you know why? What is the recommended cluster size?
I've formatted different microSD cards using the default Windows settings. All were successfully recognized.
Hi, I tested FAT32 with the default cluster size but it didn't work. Then I tried FAT32 with a 4092-byte cluster size and it worked well. Not sure why – any ideas?
I tested formatting a 2GB microSD card and found the cluster size defaults to 4096 bytes (4KB). [product_name] works with the card formatted this way.
Thank you. What happens if you use a cluster size of 1024 bytes or 32KB? Will it work regardless of cluster size? Thanks.
I'm not sure, and don't see a need to test. The default settings have always worked for me.

Hi, Wikipedia provides good explanations on the differences. The default cluster size depends on your operating system when formatting an MSD card. If you use operating systems like MacOS or Linux, there may be more variations. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are sharing their experiences with microSD card compatibility and formatting for [product_name]. The main issues discussed include which card types and sizes are supported, proper file system (FAT32), and cluster size settings. Some users encountered problems when using default formatting, while others found that alternative cluster sizes (such as 4096 bytes) worked. The information provided by [company_name] support indicates limited official support for certain card types, contributing to mixed findings and a lack of universally recognized solutions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect clear compatibility guidelines that specify supported microSD card types, sizes, and formatting requirements—especially cluster size—to ensure reliable operation with [product_name].
